classification.difficultyReason: The student must interpret changes and stationary intervals on three displacement–time graphs.

content.prompt: Match the scenario with each of the displacement–time graphs below.

spec.description: Graph (I): displacement rises linearly from zero and immediately falls linearly to zero.
spec.mathematics: A two-lap out-and-back journey without a stationary interval.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and label are visible in the question.

spec.description: Graph (II): displacement rises linearly, remains constant briefly, then falls linearly to zero.
spec.mathematics: Move away, rest at positive displacement, then return to the start.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and label are visible in the question.

spec.description: Graph (III): displacement rises, returns to zero, remains zero briefly, then rises again.
spec.mathematics: Move away, return to the start, pause, then move away again.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and label are visible in the question.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Bob walks down the street and realises he has forgotten his wallet. He turns around, jogs back home to get it, then walks back down the street again.

answer.worked: (III). Bob walks away from home, returns to displacement zero, then walks away again. The brief horizontal segment at zero allows time to collect his wallet.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Mary practises for a 100-metre sprint. After the first run, she rests for a moment at the finish line, then walks back to the start position again.

answer.worked: (II). Mary's displacement rises during the sprint, stays constant while she rests at the finish, then falls to zero as she walks back.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Jane swims two laps of a 50-metre pool non-stop.

answer.worked: (I). Jane swims to the far end of the pool and immediately returns to her starting position, with no resting interval.
